items.q: The pathophysiology chain starts with endothelial damage, which next causes:
opts: VWF release and platelet plug formation
items.exp: Endothelial damage → VWF release → platelet plug formation. (Book p754)

items.q: Fill up: In the TMA flowchart, platelets trapped in the plug produce ______.
items.exp: Platelet trapped in plug → thrombocytopenia. (Book p754)

items.q: Schistocyte formation and hence MAHA arise because:
opts: Circulating erythrocytes are damaged by the platelet plug
Autoantibodies lyse the red cell membrane
Fibrin strands are absent from the microvessels
items.exp: Schistocyte formation d/t platelet plug circulating erythrocytes damage → MAHA. (Book p754)

items.q: Typical/childhood HUS accounts for what proportion of cases?

Match each toxin with its organism — 1) Shiga like toxin / verocytotoxin 2) Shiga toxin 3) Neuraminidase toxin … A) Shigella dysentery B) Streptococcus pneumoniae C) Enterohemorrhagic E. coli (O157:H7)
items.exp: Shiga like toxin/verocytotoxin – EHEC O157:H7; Shiga toxin – Shigella dysentery; neuraminidase toxin – Streptococcus pneumoniae. (Book p754)
